add_nodes.title: A Mars lander flies proof-checked landing and fault logic
add_nodes.description: A lander reaches the surface of Mars flying entry, descent and landing guidance and fault-management logic whose key properties are machine-checked: sensor gating, mode switches, engine and reboot logic, and guidance numerics, with assumptions red-teamed against Mars atmosphere and terrain models. The team says so publicly. Any Mars lander counts, from a 20 t Starship to a small commercial lander.
add_nodes.status_oct2026: No lander has reached Mars since 2021. Launch windows: late 2026, Dec 2028-Jan 2029, early 2031, about Apr 2033 and about mid-2035, so landings inside the horizon come in late 2029, late 2031 and late 2033. Landers already scheduled for 2028, such as ESA's Rosalind Franklin rover, fix their software before proof agents mature (general). Schiaparelli (2016) crashed when a saturated inertial unit led its software to compute a negative altitude.
add_nodes.why: Mars is where proof-checked autonomy matters most. One-way light time of 3-22 minutes rules out ground help during a descent of about 7 minutes, and Schiaparelli shows that one wrong assumption in fault logic loses a lander. The clock is the window. Chain (S2): toolchain 2028 and per-flight re-proof at the reusable launch operator 2029 -> that operator's first Mars landing, late 2031 from the early-2031 window, carries re-proved landing and fault logic, since its software changes between flights -> 2031 at the earliest. A new government lander needs a freeze 12-18 months before launch and lands in the 2033 window. S3 is the same year because windows and the operator's choices bind. S1: 2033. The 2035 window lands in 2036, past the horizon. Bands: this is a joint event. A Mars landing by 2035 is Medium (hyper-mars-heavy-landing), the likeliest carrier may not use or disclose proofs, and no funded non-Starship lander targets 2031 or 2033, so S2-S4 are Low by 2035 and Speculative by 2031. Mars truth data is scarce (about 10 successful landings ever), so the lunar-derived envelopes in verif-environment-assumption-models transfer only partly.
add_nodes.strongest_case_small: Mars landings stay rare through 2035, perhaps a handful, and most risk sits in entry physics, supersonic retropropulsion and hardware, which proofs do not touch. The lead candidate builds confidence through flight and may never say what it proved.
add_nodes.signpost: A Mars lander team, commercial or government, stating in a press kit, paper or review that its descent guidance and fault logic are machine-checked, for the 2031 or 2033 window.
add_nodes.note_2035: New node: the late-2031 and late-2033 Mars landings fall inside the horizon, but a landing, proof-checked logic and public disclosure must all happen, so it stays Low. S4 equals S3 because launch windows and landing physics bind, and robots add nothing to either.
add_nodes.revision_note: E-verified-autonomy (2035 horizon, S4): added for the 2035 horizon. Hard edge from verif-lander-verified-gnc-flight; soft from hyper-mars-heavy-landing (any Mars lander counts), environment envelopes, optimizer certificates, certified EDL guidance and per-flight re-proof. | E-verified-autonomy resolver (2026-10-07): advocate's S2 2033 -> 2031 accepted: the likeliest carrier re-proves software between flights, so the new-program freeze does not bind (the reasoning B-round used for verif-rpo-assured-autonomy); soft edge from verif-launch-fsw-per-flight added. Skeptic's joint-event bands accepted: band_2031 S3-S4 Low -> Speculative, band_2035 S1 Low -> Speculative and S2-S4 Medium -> Low (Medium landing odds times adoption times disclosure gives about 0.1-0.3). S2 now equals S3. Thesis changed to Low.

add_nodes.title: Space processor flies with proven timing isolation
add_nodes.description: A radiation-tolerant multicore processor or SoC flies on an operational mission with machine-checked proofs that flight software keeps its worst-case timing whatever runs on the other cores, including an onboard AI payload. This closes the gap left by today's verified stacks, where spatial isolation is proven and timing interference is only measured.
add_nodes.status_oct2026: Multicore timing interference is measured and argued, and aviation accepts that evidence through FAA AC 20-193 and EASA AMC 20-193 (general). No flight processor has a proof of it. seL4 proves spatial isolation, and its time-protection work is research (general). verif-verified-onboard-stack and verif-onboard-ai-guardrails both name measured timing as their open gap.
add_nodes.why: Orbital compute and onboard agents put AI payloads on the same processor as flight software, and this branch's verified-stack and guardrail nodes stop where timing is measured. Proving timing needs a processor designed for analyzable timing (partitioned caches, a predictable interconnect) plus RTL proofs, which hardware proof agents make cheap. Fabrication runs of 3-4 months, scarce heavy-ion beam time and 1-2 years of qualification do not compress, and after qualification, design-in and spacecraft integration add about a year before an operational flight. Chain (S2): hardware proof agents 2028 -> a timing-predictable design proved 2029-30 -> tape-out and radiation test 2030-31 -> qualification 2031-33 -> first operational flight 2034. S3 is a year earlier, 2033, because its AI-designed processors come a year sooner (capability-ai-eda-space-processor). S1 lands after 2035. Bands: Medium by 2035 in S3-S4, where near-free RTL proofs let any new space processor carry them and onboard agents create mixed-criticality demand. Low in S2, because most operators accept measured isolation or use separate processors.
add_nodes.strongest_case_small: Operators can put flight software and AI on separate processors, which costs little mass at orbital-compute scale, and aviation already certifies multicore systems on measured evidence. A proven-timing processor may stay a niche part.
add_nodes.signpost: A space processor vendor or agency program releasing a part with formal timing-isolation proofs; a flight announcement that cites them.
add_nodes.note_2035: New node: a second-generation item that closes the timing gap the verified onboard stack leaves open, reachable in 2033-34. S4 equals S3 because fabs, beam time and qualification bind, and none is labor-bound.
add_nodes.revision_note: E-verified-autonomy (2035 horizon, S4): added for the 2035 horizon. Hard edges from verif-hardware-proof-agents and verif-verified-onboard-stack; soft from capability-ai-eda-space-processor and verif-onboard-ai-guardrails (demand). | E-verified-autonomy resolver (2026-10-07): skeptic's changes accepted: S2 2033 -> 2034 and S3-S4 2032 -> 2033 (the draft fused qualification and first operational flight into one year), band_2031 S3-S4 Low -> Speculative (the year is after 2031), band_2035 S2 Medium -> Low (thin demand: separate processors are cheap and AC 20-193 accepts measured evidence). Resolver: band_2035 S1 Low -> Speculative, since S1 has no chain inside the horizon.

add_nodes.title: Flight-software standards write in credit for AI proofs
add_nodes.description: A flight-software or assurance standard names AI-written, checker-verified proofs as an accepted verification method, so programs no longer argue the route plan by plan. Examples: a revision of NASA's NPR 7150.2 or NASA-STD-8739.8, an ECSS software standard, or an RTCA/EUROCAE update to DO-333.
add_nodes.status_oct2026: DO-333 (2011) gives aviation credit for formal methods, and NPR 7150.2D (2022) and ECSS software standards permit them. No standard mentions AI-generated proofs. DO-178B came in 1992 and DO-178C in 2011. NPR 7150.2 revisions came in 2014, 2019 and 2022 (general). RCC 319 editions came in September 2014, July 2019 and June 2025 (RCC 319-25, Range Commanders Council, posted on the TRMC site).
add_nodes.why: Plan-by-plan acceptance (infra-tool-qualification) sets precedent; a standard makes it the default and lets suppliers and small teams use the route without a bespoke argument. Standards bodies revise on 3-10 year cycles and usually codify practice after several programs have used it. Chain (S2): first plan acceptance 2030 -> completed certifications that bank the credit 2032-34 -> several programs on the route and the next revision of a NASA, ESA, RTCA or RCC document naming it 2034. S3 is a year earlier, 2033. S1 lands after 2035. Bands: S3-S4 Medium by 2035 because several bodies each revise inside the window; S2 Low because it reaches several programs only in 2033-34. No revision that addresses AI proofs is in motion today, so the cap holds at Medium.
add_nodes.strongest_case_small: Standards may never single out AI. The checker-not-generator route already fits DO-333 and DO-330, so bodies can leave it to guidance material and individual plans, and this node would never be marked achieved even as practice changes.
add_nodes.signpost: A draft revision of NPR 7150.2, NASA-STD-8739.8, an ECSS software standard or DO-333 that mentions machine-generated proofs; an RTCA or EUROCAE committee taking up the topic.
add_nodes.note_2035: New node: codifying the route becomes reachable in 2033-34 once several programs have banked credit. S4 equals S3 because committees, comment periods and revision cycles are institutional clocks.
add_nodes.revision_note: E-verified-autonomy (2035 horizon, S4): added for the 2035 horizon. Hard edge from infra-tool-qualification; soft from the credibility-evidence standard, regulator AI capacity and the crewed certification precedent. | E-verified-autonomy resolver (2026-10-07): skeptic's changes accepted: S2 2033 -> 2034 and S3-S4 2032 -> 2033 (the node's own codify-after-several-programs logic and the 2-4-year certification lag in infra-tool-qualification), band_2035 S1 Low -> Speculative and S2 Medium -> Low; removed from the spine because it may never be marked achieved. RCC 319-25 (June 2025) checked and cited; NPR 7150.2 cadence added.

add_nodes.title: Flight-software verification takes half the calendar time
add_nodes.description: At a leading space firm, the calendar time to fully verify a safety-critical flight-software release, including proofs, hardware-in-the-loop runs and integrated vehicle regression, falls to half its 2026 level, and the firm, a customer or an agency review reports it. Proof work stops being the long pole by about 2029; this node needs the physical test slice to shrink as well.
add_nodes.status_oct2026: Proof and unit verification are a large share of software cost, but hardware-in-the-loop rigs and integrated tests set release pace at most programs (general). astro-gnc-assurance-cost expects only a 20-30% cut in verification calendar time in S2 for that reason. Starliner's 2019 software errors were catchable by the end-to-end integrated test the program did not run (general).
add_nodes.why: Once proofs are cheap, hardware-in-the-loop rigs and integrated vehicle tests set the verification calendar. Halving it needs that slice to shrink: more rigs (capital), AI-run sequencing (S3) and, in S4, general-purpose robots that reconfigure rigs, swap units and run integrated vehicle tests around the clock. Sketch (assumptions: rigs and integrated tests are about 80% of calendar time, and proofs cut the rest to 0.1-0.15 of 2026). S2: test compresses 1.2-1.4x by 2035, so the calendar ends near 0.6-0.7 of 2026 and never halves. S3: test at 0.60-0.69 of 2026 by 2035 gives 0.50-0.58, half only at the edge in 2035. S4 at robot-first firms: if half the test slice is robot-bound vehicle testing (2.1-2.8x by 2035 in embodied/research-space.json, less a quarter for adoption and requalification) and half is real-time HIL rig time at about 1.6x, the calendar reaches 0.48-0.54 in 2032 and 0.44-0.50 by 2035. Chain (S4): robot-run integration and test at a robot-first firm 2031 -> half the calendar at the optimistic edge 2032 -> one full release cycle and a report 2033. S3: AI-run rigs alone reach half only in 2035. Bands: S4 Medium by 2035 because its central case sits just under half but must be measured and reported; S3 Low because only its edge case reaches half.
add_nodes.strongest_case_small: Leading firms already release flight software fast by flying often, so the change may not be measurable, and firms rarely publish verification calendars. Real-time HIL and soak runs do not shorten with robots, and requalifying robot-run test processes costs 6-24 months before any gain.
add_nodes.signpost: A launch or spacecraft operator reporting release verification time, hardware-in-the-loop and integrated tests included, at half its earlier level; robot-run integration and test at a leading space firm.
add_nodes.note_2035: The one place in this branch where S4 differs: robot-run vehicle tests at robot-first firms give S4 2033 and Medium against S3 2035 and Low, a larger credit than the usual 0.5-1.5 years because ground test is about 80% of the remaining calendar. It needs robo-24x7-integration-test (S4 2031), a requalified test process and one full release cycle before a firm can report.
add_nodes.revision_note: E-verified-autonomy (2035 horizon, S4): added for the 2035 horizon. Hard edge from astro-gnc-assurance-cost; soft from AI-run test stands, per-flight re-proof and robo-24x7-integration-test. S4 credit under the four-condition rule. | E-verified-autonomy resolver (2026-10-07): years S2 2034 -> >2035, S3 2033 -> 2035, S4 2032 -> 2033; band_2035 S2 Low -> Speculative, S3 Medium -> Low, S4 Medium kept. Skeptic: the draft's own sketch left S3 near 0.55 by 2035 and S2 at 0.6-0.7, so neither halves at the draft's years; real-time HIL time is only partly robot-bound; the robo-requal-standard soft edge duplicated robo-24x7-integration-test's prerequisite chain and is dropped. Skeptic's S4 2034 and Low rejected: read at the same optimistic edge as S3, S4 crosses half in 2032 and reports in 2033, and its central case is under half by 2035. Advocate: reporting widened to a customer or agency review (accepted); S4 High rejected, because only part of the test slice is robot-bound and reporting is uncertain; S3 2033 rejected by its own arithmetic (0.51 in 2035). Soft edge from struct-35-qual-campaigns-30pct-shorter not added: it shares the mechanism, it does not cause this node.

patch.thesis: Verified flight code gets 15-120x cheaper per line by 2028-29 and flies on landers and constellations about 2029 (base case). By 2035 certifiers accept AI-written proofs (High); crewed credit stays Medium and a proof-checked Mars landing is Low. S4 adds about two years on one node: robot-run ground tests halve the verification calendar at robot-first firms about 2033.
